function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run in a script).  
I’ve also included the exact file contents that you’ll need to create/modify.  
> **NOTE** – I can’t actually run `git clone`, `git push`, etc. from here, but the commands below will do it for you on your machine.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & create/update files

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create or overwrite `Dockerfile` in the repo root:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image
FROM python:3.8-slim

# Maintainer
LABEL maintainer="Unknown"

# Install system deps (if any)
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files
COPY package*.json ./

# Install npm dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why `python:3.8-slim`?**  
> The tool defaults to that image; it’s lightweight and works fine for a Node.js app.  
> If you prefer a Node base image, just change the `FROM` line to `node:18-alpine`.

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAMLs

Create a directory `k8s` (or use the repo root) and add `deployment.yaml`:

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry/tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **Tip** – If you’re pushing the image to GitHub Container Registry, change the image name to  
> `ghcr.io/<your-username>/nodejs-welcome:latest`.

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout repo
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Log in to Docker Hub (or GHCR)
      - name: Log in to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build and push
      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- adjust if using GHCR

      # Optional: create a release tag
      - name: Create Release Tag
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: |
          git tag -a v$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S) -m "Release $(date +%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S)"
          git push origin --tags
```

> **Secrets required**  
> * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub username  
> * `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a Docker Hub access token (or use `GHCR_TOKEN` if pushing to GHCR)

---

## 3️⃣ Add all changed files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

---

### Quick sanity check

```bash
# Verify Dockerfile builds locally
docker build -t nodejs-welcome:local .

# Verify Kubernetes manifests apply (requires a cluster)
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

---

## 🎉 Done!

You now have:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a container image for the Node.js app |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys the app to Kubernetes (2 replicas, ClusterIP service) |
| `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes the image on every push to `main` |

Feel free to tweak the image names, tags, or Kubernetes settings to match your environment. Happy coding!
